ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Classifying the junctional rate

A stable adult has a regular narrow-complex rhythm at 78/min with retrograde P waves and no normal sinus P waves. The clinician identifies an AV-junctional pacemaker. Which rate-based term best describes this rhythm?

  1. Accelerated junctional rhythm
  2. Junctional escape rhythm at its usual intrinsic rate
  3. Junctional tachycardia
  4. Sinus bradycardia
  5. Ventricular fibrillation
Answer and explanation

Accelerated junctional rhythm

A junctional rate approximately 60–100/min is conventionally termed accelerated junctional rhythm.

Option explanations

Accelerated junctional rhythm: A junctional rate approximately 60–100/min is conventionally termed accelerated junctional rhythm.

Junctional escape rhythm at its usual intrinsic rate: Typical junctional escape rates are approximately 40–60/min.

Junctional tachycardia: Junctional tachycardia generally exceeds 100/min in adult rate classification.

Sinus bradycardia: Retrograde rather than sinus P waves identify a non-sinus origin.

Ventricular fibrillation: Fibrillation lacks organized narrow complexes.
